An [Arazzo](https://spec.openapis.org/arazzo/latest.html) document describes **workflows**:
sequences of API calls, each step calling an operation of an OpenAPI (or, in Arazzo 1.1, AsyncAPI)
description, with the inputs a workflow takes, the outputs it returns, and what happens when a step
succeeds or fails. Apiome treats Arazzo **1.0.x** and **1.1.x** as first-class: you can bring a
workflow in with the API files it calls, read it as a flow, check that every step points at a real
operation, compare two revisions, export it back, and run it against a deployment or a mock.

Each part has its own page. This page shows how they fit together.

## When to use it

- **You document how an API is meant to be used, not only what it offers.** A checkout, an
  onboarding or an adopt-a-pet flow lives next to the APIs it calls, with its steps resolved to their
  operations.
- **A workflow must keep working as its APIs change.** A change to a workflow's inputs, outputs,
  criteria or sources is graded like any other breaking change, and a stored workflow can be run in
  CI against a mock or a staging deployment.
- **Agents or partners follow your workflows.** The steps, their success criteria and their outputs
  are readable from the UI, the CLI and the REST API.

## The lifecycle at a glance

| You want to… | Where | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Bring in** a workflow with the OpenAPI and AsyncAPI files it calls | **Import** dialog, or `apiome import arazzo <archive or folder>` | [Import an Arazzo workflow with its API files](../bring-in/import-a-spec.md#import-an-arazzo-workflow-with-its-api-files) |
| **Read** its steps, inputs, outputs and success and failure paths | The **Workflows** tab of a catalog item or project; `apiome arazzo list` and `apiome arazzo show` | [Arazzo workflows](./arazzo-workflows.mdx) |
| **Check** that every step resolved and every source was found | `apiome arazzo validate`, or `apiome arazzo validate FILE` for a local document | [Arazzo workflow records](../reference/arazzo-workflow-records.md) |
| **Lint** its structure — expressions, criteria, `goto` targets, ids, inputs and outputs | The **Quality** score of the revision; `GET /v1/lint/rules` lists the rules | [Lint rules](#lint-rules) |
| **Compare** two revisions and see what breaks a workflow's callers | `apiome diff`, the diff GitHub Action, the publish check and catalog change reports | [Arazzo workflow changes](../ship/api-changelog.mdx#arazzo-workflow-changes) |
| **Export** it back, or start workflows for an API you already have | **Export** dialog → **REST & HTTP** → **Arazzo** | [Arazzo from any source](../ship/export-a-spec.md#arazzo-from-any-source), [Arazzo exports](../ship/export-fidelity.md#arazzo) |
| **Run** it, step by step, against a deployment or a mock | `apiome arazzo run <workflowId> --target <target>` | [Run a workflow against a target](./arazzo-workflows.mdx#run-a-workflow-against-a-target) |

## Arazzo 1.0 and 1.1

Every surface accepts both lines and keeps the version a document declares:

- **Import and validation** check a document against the JSON Schema for its own version, 1.0.x or
  1.1.x, so a 1.1 document is not judged by 1.0 rules.
- **Arazzo 1.1 additions** come in and go back out unchanged: AsyncAPI source descriptions, steps
  that wait on an event channel (`channelPath`, with `action`, `correlationId` and `timeout`),
  workflow-level `parameters`, `querystring` parameters and `$self`.
- **Export** writes 1.0 or 1.1 as you choose. A workflow with AsyncAPI sources needs 1.1, because
  1.0 cannot express them; asking for 1.0 is refused rather than silently dropping the sources.
- **Round trips are tested** against the OpenAPI Initiative's own examples and files from Redocly,
  Spectral and Specmatic; the fidelity report on the **Arazzo** card names any difference.

## Lint rules

Every Arazzo revision is linted by the `arazzo` rule pack, under the rules of the version it
declares. All of these are **errors** by default; a style guide can turn any of them down or off.

| The pack checks that… | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| each step's `operationId` or `operationRef` names an operation of a declared source | [`arazzo.dangling-operation-id`](./lint-rules.md#arazzo-dangling-operation-id), [`arazzo.unresolvable-operation-ref`](./lint-rules.md#arazzo-unresolvable-operation-ref) |
| every `$`-expression parses — the finding gives the position where it stops | [`arazzo.runtime-expression-invalid`](./lint-rules.md#arazzo-runtime-expression-invalid) |
| a `jsonpath` or `regex` success criterion names its `context` | [`arazzo.success-criteria-context-required`](./lint-rules.md#arazzo-success-criteria-context-required) |
| a `goto` action's `stepId` or `workflowId` exists | [`arazzo.on-success-target-unresolved`](./lint-rules.md#arazzo-on-success-target-unresolved), [`arazzo.on-failure-target-unresolved`](./lint-rules.md#arazzo-on-failure-target-unresolved) |
| every `$components.*` reference names a declared component | [`arazzo.component-ref-unresolved`](./lint-rules.md#arazzo-component-ref-unresolved) |
| step ids are unique in their workflow, and workflow ids in the document | [`arazzo.step-id-duplicate`](./lint-rules.md#arazzo-step-id-duplicate), [`arazzo.workflow-id-duplicate`](./lint-rules.md#arazzo-workflow-id-duplicate) |
| workflow `dependsOn` chains do not loop back | [`arazzo.depends-on-cycle`](./lint-rules.md#arazzo-depends-on-cycle) |
| a parameter's `in` is one its step's source defines: `path`, `query`, `header` or `cookie` for OpenAPI (plus `querystring` in 1.1); `header` or `channel` for an AsyncAPI step | [`arazzo.parameter-in-invalid`](./lint-rules.md#arazzo-parameter-in-invalid) |
| workflow `inputs` are valid JSON Schema 2020-12 | [`arazzo.inputs-schema-invalid`](./lint-rules.md#arazzo-inputs-schema-invalid) |
| every output is a runtime expression (or, from 1.1, a selector object) | [`arazzo.outputs-expression-invalid`](./lint-rules.md#arazzo-outputs-expression-invalid) |
| each source description's `type` is one the version defines — `asyncapi` only from 1.1 | [`arazzo.source-description-type-invalid`](./lint-rules.md#arazzo-source-description-type-invalid), [`arazzo.async-source-before-1-1`](./lint-rules.md#arazzo-async-source-before-1-1) |

Two **warnings** round out the pack:
[`arazzo.missing-success-criteria`](./lint-rules.md#arazzo-missing-success-criteria) and
[`arazzo.unused-workflow-input`](./lint-rules.md#arazzo-unused-workflow-input).

The operationRef rule shipped as `arzzo.unresolvable-operation-ref`. Findings now carry
`arazzo.unresolvable-operation-ref`, and the old id is kept as an **alias**: a style guide that
names it, a stored finding and a waiver recorded against it all still match.

## How the pieces fit

1. **Import stores the workflow as records.** Each workflow and each of its steps is stored on the
   revision, and each step's `operationId` or `operationRef` is matched to the operation it calls —
   in the same archive or repository selection, in a spec already in the catalog, or fetched from
   its URL. A step that matches nothing is kept as written and marked **unresolved**, with the
   reason; so is a source description nothing could find.
2. **Every read uses those records.** The **Workflows** tab, `apiome arazzo list|show|validate`
   and the `GET /v1/workflows/…` routes all read the same workflows, steps and resolution states.
3. **Changes are graded by workflow rules.** Comparing two revisions grades each change by what a
   workflow's callers depend on: a newly required input or a removed output is **Breaking**, a
   changed success criterion is flagged for review, an added optional input is **Safe**. A change
   no rule covers is reported as breaking.
4. **A run sends the steps in order.** `apiome arazzo run` builds each request from the inputs and
   earlier steps' outputs, judges each step's success criteria with expected and actual values, and
   follows `goto`, `retry` and `end`. It sends only `GET`, `HEAD` and `OPTIONS` steps unless the
   target allows writes, the run opts in, and a fixture names the operation. Every run is recorded
   as verification evidence.

## From the command line

```bash
apiome import arazzo ./checkout.zip --dry-run                       # what would come in
apiome import arazzo ./checkout/ --root checkout.arazzo.yaml
apiome arazzo list --catalog <item-uuid>                            # workflows and resolution
apiome arazzo show checkout --catalog <item-uuid>
apiome arazzo validate checkout.arazzo.yaml                         # local schema check
apiome arazzo validate --catalog <item-uuid>                        # exit 7 when a step did not resolve
apiome arazzo run checkout --catalog <item-uuid> --target checkout-mock --input cartId=42
```

See [`apiome arazzo`](../reference/cli/arazzo.md) and
[`apiome import arazzo`](../reference/cli/import.md#import-arazzo) in the CLI reference, and
[Arazzo workflows](../reference/rest/arazzo-workflows.md) in the REST reference.
